title: References to send before a first call
metaTitle: Three references and why they matter
excerpt: Send three sites before a first call, each with one sentence on why it matters. A folder of fifty links asks the studio to guess your taste, and that guess will miss.
alt: A dim desk with an iMac showing a code editor beside a portfolio page, a second monitor with a mountain wallpaper, and a lit lamp. Two screens of references, which is already plenty for a first call.
caption: A desk with the work up, and the lamp on. Photograph via Unsplash.

faqs.question: How many references should you send a studio?
faqs.answer: Send three live URLs, each with one sentence you wrote about why it is relevant. One link is only a mood, and fifty is a refusal to choose. Mark a negative example as negative, or the studio will treat it as a wish. If you cannot write the sentence, pick a different site.

faqs.question: What makes a useful sentence?
faqs.answer: Name a decision the studio can see: the type, the density, the first screen, the path to the product. Premium and vibe are conclusions, not evidence. Say whether you are taking the whole page or only one principle, especially when you cannot afford the photography the reference depends on.

faqs.question: What should the studio do with the three links?
faqs.answer: Open them before the call, including on a phone, and test your sentences against the pages. If two links contradict each other, ask which role each one plays. References are evidence, not orders. A pixel match of someone else's site is a bad goal for your buyer.

sources.title: How Long Do Users Stay on Web Pages?
Influencing your title links in Google Search

markdown:
Design studio references should arrive as three sites and one sentence on why each is relevant. A folder of fifty links asks the studio to guess your taste. The guess will be wrong in a way that wastes the first call, because the studio will prepare for a project you did not mean.

Send the three before the call, in the same note as the time. The call can then start from the sentences, not from a tour of the internet.

## Why three is enough

Three is enough to show a range without hiding. One reference is a mood. Fifty is a refusal to choose. Three forces you to say what you actually want repeated: a kind of type, a kind of density, a kind of shop, a kind of product screen.

Each link needs a sentence you wrote, not a compliment you copied from their homepage. “This product page names the object and the price in the first screen, which is the pace we want.” “This editorial site keeps a long essay readable, which matters because our story is a text, not a poster.” “We do not want this navigation. Sending it so you can see the clutter we are leaving.” The negative example is allowed if you mark it as negative. An unmarked negative example will be treated as a wish.

People judge a page quickly. Nielsen Norman Group’s 2011 article on [how long users stay](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/how-long-do-users-stay-on-web-pages/) notes that users often leave within 10 to 20 seconds, and that a clear value proposition in those first 10 seconds earns more time. Your sentence should say what you noticed in that first glance, because that is also what your customers will notice. “I like the vibe” does not survive the glance. “The first screen says who it is for” does.

If you cannot write the sentence, you are not ready to send the link. Look again, or pick a different site. The exercise is the point. It teaches you your own brief.

## What to send, and what to leave out

Send live URLs. A screenshot of a homepage from two years ago will be designed against, and then you will be disappointed when the studio matches a page that no longer exists. If the thing you love is a specific interior page, send that URL, not the root.

Leave out the password-protected deck, the fifty-slide brand book, and the Pinterest board, unless a single frame in them is one of the three. A board is a mood with no decisions. The studio can make a beautiful average of a board. You will not know why you dislike it, because the board never had to choose.

Leave out competitors you want to beat but do not want to resemble. Say the competitor in a different sentence: “They are who buyers compare us to. We should be clearly not their layout.” That is strategy. It is not a visual reference. Mixing the two makes a clone with a different logo.

You may include one of your own past pages, with a sentence about what must change. “Our current homepage buries the product. Keep the name, replace the structure.” That is often the most useful link in the three, because it is constrained by reality.

Google’s guidance on [title links](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/title-link) is a small test you can apply while you pick. A reference with a title that says what the page is will be easier for your customers too. If every site you love has a mysterious title and a mysterious first screen, notice that you are collecting puzzles. Say whether you want the puzzle or only the craft.

## How specific the sentence should be

Aim at a decision the studio can keep or refuse.

Type and reading. “Long text, comfortable measure, almost no decoration.” Or “short lines, large type, one idea per screen.” These are different products.

Photography versus interface. “The object is the hero, UI stays quiet.” Or “the screen is a tool, density is fine, as on a trading view.” Trade Moai, a public Hanabi trading interface concept, is an example of density with a job. A calm brand site such as Wabisabi is the other direction. You might respect both and still need to say which one this project is.

Commerce. “A shop that feels like a room, not a marketplace grid.” Down the Cove’s public work is an ecommerce migration and redesign, useful if your problem is a store, and a distraction if your problem is a single essay.

Proof. “Show one real project in depth, not a logo wall.” If that is the sentence, the studio knows what to design and what to decline when someone later asks for the logo wall.

Do not send a sentence the studio cannot see. “It feels premium” is not visible. “Lots of whitespace, a serif for headlines, and no stock photography of handshakes” is visible. Premium is the conclusion. The sentence should be the evidence.

## What the studio should do with them

Read the three before the call. Open them on a phone as well as a desk. Note where your sentences match the pages and where they do not. If you say a page is calm and the page autoplays a loud film, the studio should say so. References are not orders. They are evidence. The studio’s job is to test the evidence against the goal.

Bring questions, not a mood board in reply. “Your first link is a publication and your third is a dense app. The brief says you sell one product to operators. The third link is the closer match. Did you mean the first as a writing standard only?” That question saves a month. A studio that only says the references are lovely has not started the work.

Do not widen the three into a scavenger hunt. Asking the founder for twenty more examples moves the decision back onto them after they already did the hard part. If something is missing, ask one precise question. “Do you have a reference for the empty state, or should we propose it?”

During the call, share a screen and look at one of the three for five minutes. Talk about the first screen, the type, and the path to contact or to the product. You will learn more than from a portfolio reel. The reel is the studio’s editing. The reference is yours.

## Taste, constraints, and honesty

A reference you cannot afford is still useful if you say what you are taking. “We want that kind of photography and we do not have that budget. We will design for type and a small set of pictures we can shoot.” The sentence prevents a proposal that assumes a photoshoot you will cancel in week three.

A reference from a famous company is fine as a standard for one detail and dangerous as a plan for the whole. You do not have their brand equity. Your first screen has to explain more than theirs does. Say that so the studio does not copy the opacity.

If the three contradict each other, notice before you send them. Two calm editorial sites and one maximalist shop, with no note, read as indecision. Either pick a direction or label the roles. “One and two are tone. Three is only the cart, which is the interaction we need to keep.” Roles make contradictions usable.

You are also a reference. The way you write the note is a sample of the voice. A careful, specific note gets a careful response. A dump of links with “thoughts?” gets a generic deck, because that is all the note made possible.

Keep the three in the project thread. When feedback later says “make it more like the references,” you can ask “which sentence?” The original words stop the project from sliding toward a vague memory of a website someone liked in a meeting.

## What not to expect from the exercise

The studio will not become the team that shipped your reference. They should be able to say what they will take from it and what they will not copy. A pixel match is a bad goal. It is also often a trademark problem and a strategic one. You want the principle, on your content, for your buyer.

Do not send references the night before and expect them to be studied. A day or two is enough for three sites. If the call is sooner, bring two and look at them together, and send the third after. Looking together beats a performance of preparation that did not happen.

If you are the studio receiving fifty links, reply with the constraint. “Send three, each with a sentence, before Friday. We will use those in the call.” You are not being difficult. You are refusing to guess. Founders usually feel relief, because the folder was a way to postpone a choice they were willing to make once someone asked.

After the references, the work of a brand sprint has to leave something a website can use. [The work a brand sprint should leave behind](/blog/the-work-a-brand-sprint-should-leave-behind) is the next piece. A sentence, a small palette, type, and a logo that works small will do more for the build than another folder of links.

When you are ready to show those three sites to a studio, the place to start is [Hanabi’s services](https://tryhanabi.com/#services). The useful first conversation is about which of the three principles belong in the site you are actually building.
